title: 1 Kings 4
paragraphs: ¹ King Solomon ruled over all Israel. ² These were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok — the priest; ³ Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha — secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud — recorder; ⁴ Benaiah son of Jehoiada — commander of the army; Zadok and Abiathar — priests; ⁵ Azariah son of Nathan — in charge of the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan — a priest and personal adviser to the king;

⁶ Ahishar — palace administrator; Adoniram son of Abda — in charge of forced labor. ⁷ Solomon also had twelve district governors over all Israel who supplied provisions for the king and the royal household. Each man was responsible for one month of the year. ⁸ These were their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim; ⁹ Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Bethhanan; ¹⁰ Ben-Hesed, in Aruboth — he had Socoh and all the land of Hepher;

¹¹ Ben-Abinadab, in the whole region of Dor — he was married to Taphath, Solomon's daughter; ¹² Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and in all of Beth Shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shean to Abel Meholah as far as Jokmeam; ¹³ Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead — he had the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead, and the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty large walled cities with bronze gate bars; ¹⁴ Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim; ¹⁵ Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he too had married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath;

¹⁶ Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Aloth; ¹⁷ Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar; ¹⁸ Shimei son of Elah, in Benjamin; ¹⁹ Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead — the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and the country of Og king of Bashan — and he was the only governor over the district. ²⁰ The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They ate and drank and were happy.

²¹ Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms paid tribute and were subject to Solomon all his life. ²² Solomon's daily provisions were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal, ²³ ten head of stall-fed cattle, twenty head of pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep and goats — plus deer, gazelles, roebucks, and choice poultry. ²⁴ For he ruled over all the region west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the river. He had peace on all sides. ²⁵ Throughout Solomon's lifetime, Judah and Israel lived in safety, everyone under their own vine and fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba.

²⁶ Solomon had four thousand stalls for chariot horses and twelve thousand horsemen. ²⁷ These district governors supplied provisions for King Solomon and for all who came to the king's table, each in his assigned month. They made sure nothing was lacking. ²⁸ They also brought the required amounts of barley and straw for the horses and other animals to the places where they were stationed, each doing his part. ²⁹ God gave Solomon wisdom and very great insight, and a breadth of understanding as measureless as the sand on the seashore. ³⁰ Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt.

³¹ He was wiser than anyone — wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and than Heman, Kalkol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His fame spread to all the surrounding nations. ³² He composed three thousand proverbs and his songs numbered a thousand and five. ³³ He spoke about plant life, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop growing out of walls. He also spoke about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish. ³⁴ People came from all nations to listen to Solomon's wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
